paragraphs: Swamiji noticed a certain kind of person who calls himself broad-minded about religion but is really just restless. Such people jump from one teacher to the next, from one new idea to another, mainly for the thrill. Each new thing gives them a little rush of excitement, and once it wears off they go looking for the next one. Swamiji compared it to an addiction: religion becomes a kind of intellectual drug, and it never goes any deeper than that.
Then he shared a picture that Sri Ramakrishna used to describe a different kind of seeker, one who is like the pearl-oyster.

The oyster lives on the sea floor. But when the star Svati rises in the sky, it leaves its bed and floats up to the surface, its shell wide open, waiting for the rain. It drifts there patiently until it has caught one single drop of rainwater. Then it closes up, sinks all the way back down to the depths, and stays there quietly, working on that one drop until it has turned it into a beautiful pearl.
The lesson is clear: take one good idea, go deep with it, and let it slowly become something precious inside you.
learn: Endless scrolling through motivational clips, courses and new ideas can feel like growth but often isn't. Real change comes from taking one good idea and working on it quietly and steadily, long after the excitement has faded.
